## Summary

The Apollo 68080 Programmer's Reference Manual (PRM), converted for AI agents. It covers only what the 68080 adds to the 68000 family: new instructions, new forms of existing instructions, the extra registers, the AMMX and FPU extensions, and performance. For everything else the Motorola manuals apply.

## Details

### About the original

- Title: 68080 Programmer's Reference Manual, "The New Instructions". Concept by Tommo. Based on the original hardcopy PRM from Motorola, but simplified.
- Original: [`sources/official/AC68080PRM.odt`](../../../sources/official/AC68080PRM.odt). It is leading; these files are generated from it by `tools/intake/prm68080.py`.
- Tools named in the original: assembler: VASM , vasmm68k\_mot\_os3 & ASM1 beta; debugger: Devpac's "Vamped" MonAm 3.09; docs: Developer Documentation.
- Update: okt 2026

### How to read an instruction file

- **Field table**: Operation, Syntax, Short, Description, Constraints and condition codes, as on the original page.
- **Condition codes**: as in the Motorola manuals: `*` = set according to the result, `–` = not affected, `0`/`1` = always cleared/set.
- **Encoding**: one row per bit field. Word 1 is the opcode word; words 2 and up are extension words. Constant bits are in backticks.
- **Example**: register and memory contents are written as bytes, most significant first, as the original draws them in boxes of one hex digit. `.` is a box left empty in the original. The prefix names the operand role (`ea`, `vea`, `a`, `b`, `d`) and register.
- Every file ends with the differences from the 68000–68060 and DO/DON'T rules taken from the page.

### Instruction lists of the original

The original lists the instructions per unit with flags:

- `la`: LineA instruction, valid only when the Apollo bit (SR bit 11) is set. The legend under the lists adds: "Do not use, only available on cores 10280 to 10904".
- `p`: reading is not privileged on the 68080.

- Integer Instructions: addiw.l, addq bn, bank, bcc.s+, bra.s+, bsr.s+, clr.q (grayed out) la, cmp bn, cmpiw.l, dbcc.l, extub/w, lea bn, mov3q (grayed out) la, move bn, movea bn, move sr p, move16, move2, movec p, moveh, movex, moviw.l, moviw.l (grayed out) la, movs (grayed out) la, movz (grayed out) la, movz2, perm, subq bn, touch
- Ammx Instructions: bfly, bsel, c2p, load, loadi, lsdq, minterm, pack3216, packuswb, padd, pand, pandn, pavg, pcmpccb, pcmpccw, peor pnot (grayed out), pmaxb, pmaxw, pminb, pminw, pmul, pmula, por, psub, rex, store, storec, storei, storeilm, storem, storem3, tex, trans, unpack1632, vperm
- Floating Point Instructions: fdbcc.l, fmove fstorei (grayed out) floadi (grayed out), fmove(u)rz, fmovem, fadd, fdiv, fmul, fsub, fsqrt

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- This manual documents only 68080 additions and differences. Each file states its difference from the 68000–68060.

## Do / Don't

- DO look up a mnemonic in the tables above before writing 68080-specific code.
- DON'T assume a 68060 instruction behaves the same on the 68080 when it has a file here.
